text: What is left, most important first.
Problem 20.84 itself: is D5(Q)=1 for all finite 2-groups of class 3? A counterexample must have D4(Q)≠1 and order ≥211.
Order 211, ranks 5–7. Rank 5 is the bulk of the cost (about 100 CPU-days by estimate); at rank 7 the stock ANUPQ overflows.
Is there 3-torsion in D5/γ5, i.e. is Tahara's bound 6 attained? A minimal example has order ≥310, class 4, cyclic centre and at least two invariants ≥9 in Q/γ2.
The next case: Q/γ2 with two invariants ≥9, e.g. C9× C9× C3. There γ2/γ3 may have exponent 9, and the proof of Theorem 6.8 does not go through.
An exact criterion for nonterminality of groups of type (d,2,1): at 38, 190 of the 7 824 have descendants, and the known necessary conditions also hold for 573 terminal ones.
The group analogue of Theorem C: D2c-1(G)=1 for metabelian groups of class ≤ c? Open for p=2, c≥3 and for odd p, c≥ p+2.
